deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, equations or derivations. It is the title page and opening of Riemann's 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts', section I, 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik'. The Lucretius motto (De rerum natura I.50–51) is written twice. A purple editorial note reads '(Bitte mit einer neuen Seite anfangen!)', apparently an instruction for typesetting. There is also a struck-out sentence: the author is a Herbartian in psychology and epistemology (methodology and eidolology) but mostly cannot follow Herbart's philosophy of nature, ontology and synechology. Dedekind and Weber printed this text, nearly verbatim, in Riemann's Gesammelte Mathematische Werke (1876), 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts, I. Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik'.

Content, step by step:
(1) Every simple act of thought deposits something lasting and substantial in the soul. This is a 'Geistesmasse' (mind-mass). It appears as a unity but has an inner manifold, because it expresses something extended in space and time. All thinking is the formation of new Geistesmassen.
(2) Entering Geistesmassen appear as representations (Vorstellungen). Their inner state determines their quality.
(3) Geistesmassen fuse, combine or 'complicate' with one another and with older ones to definite degrees. Herbart's terms are Verschmelzung and Complication. The strength of these bonds depends mainly on inner kinship (similarity). Riemann promises to supplement Herbart's conditions.
(4) The soul is a compact, highly interconnected Geistesmasse. It grows continually. Geistesmassen are imperishable and their bonds indissoluble; only the relative strengths of the bonds change.
(5) Geistesmassen need no material carrier to persist and therefore have no seat in space. Their entry, formation and connection, however, need a material carrier, so all thinking happens at a definite place.
(6) An entering Geistesmasse excites every related Geistesmasse, more strongly the smaller the difference in quality. The excitation also spreads indirectly to masses connected with those through earlier thought processes. A mutually connected subset of related masses is therefore excited both directly and indirectly, and so relatively more strongly.
(7) Interaction between simultaneously forming Geistesmassen is conditioned by a material process between the places where they form. The next page specifies this as chemical-electrical. Newly forming masses also interact directly with those formed just before.

A modern reading, which is my gloss and not Riemann's notation: a weighted associative network. Nodes are mind-masses. Similarity-weighted direct excitation is combined with indirect excitation that propagates along stored links, so tightly interconnected clusters receive extra activation. This is a qualitative spreading-activation model. Riemann states it only in words.
errors: No mathematical steps, so nothing to check for correctness. The claims are speculative philosophy and psychology, not derivations.

Internal tension (philosophical, not a slip): Geistesmassen supposedly need no material carrier and have no seat in space, yet they arise as the expression of something spatially extended and are formed at definite places.

results.what: Theory of 'Geistesmassen': lasting mental substances formed by each act of thought, linked by similarity-dependent and history-dependent connections, with direct and indirect (spreading) excitation
results.modern_name: Herbartian associationist psychology; qualitatively akin to associative-network / spreading-activation models
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart (Psychologie als Wissenschaft, 1824–25) for the framework; spreading activation in modern form to Quillian (1960s) and Collins & Loftus (1975)

results.what: Psychophysical thesis: formation and binding of mental units require a material (nervous) process between their places, so thought is localized
results.modern_name: psychophysical parallelism / neural localization of mental processes

deep.surprise_reason: Non-mathematical philosophical text, published in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876) and well known to Riemann scholars. Its Herbartian character is explicit on the page.

checkable.asserts: Toy formalization (mine, not Riemann's): with equal direct excitation 1 for three related masses, adding one step of indirect excitation over links (masses 1 and 2 linked, mass 3 isolated) gives the linked pair more activation (2,2) than the isolated one (1). This is the page's qualitative claim that interconnected related masses are excited relatively more strongly; the expression evaluates to the zero vector.

transcription_corrections: Top-right page number '2.' is correct; the circled archival folio number '73' at right margin is not transcribed.

Lucretius line: the image appears to read 'disposta' (as in the standard text of De rerum natura I.50); the transcription is fine. The motto is written twice, once top right and once added at mid-right.
The marginal parenthetical after the struck-out Herbart sentence is uncertain. It plausibly reads '(die Spiritualisten ... oben noch versetzt)', but this should be marked doubtful.

The parenthetical beginning '(Nicht das Behalten unserer Erfahrung ...)' is largely illegible in the transcription. Readings such as 'Schnelligkeit' and 'proportional' are conjectural and should be checked against the 1876 printed edition.
In the struck-out paragraph, 'mittelbar[?] mit angeregt' seems right in sense ('mittelbar mit angeregt').
